claim.pdf_says: Index entries printed one per line with sub-entries indented beneath their main entry, e.g. 'INSPECT statement, VI-94' followed by the indented sub-entry 'Imperative statement, IV-39'
claim.markdown_says: Every entry is a bare line with no list marker, sub-entries only space-indented: 'INSPECT statement, VI-94' then '  Imperative statement, IV-39'
claim.why_it_matters: Markdown renders consecutive bare lines as one paragraph, so the whole index page collapses into one run-on line and the entry boundaries and hierarchy are lost when rendered (pages 961-962 use '- ' list items). Entries and references match the PDF; informative content.

verdict.reasoning: Rendered p968 at 300 dpi (printed page B-56, informative Index). Every entry and page reference in page-968.md matches the printed page in order (e.g. 'INSPECT statement, VI-94' / indented 'Imperative statement, IV-39', 'INTEGER function, A-44' / 'A-8, A-10, A-29', the INTO, INVALID KEY, I-O-CONTROL, I-O phrase, I-O status and JUSTIFIED groups), and the markdown keeps one entry per line with two-space indentation for sub-entries, mirroring the printed hierarchy. The claim itself concedes the entries and references match. The only complaint is how a Markdown renderer would reflow bare lines and that it is inconsistent with the '- ' list style on pages 961-962: a formatting/rendering difference that changes no content of the standard. Under the rejection rules (formatting only, no change of meaning) this is not a genuine content discrepancy.
